beats.narration: [excited] Drill through a marble — and through the Earth. [pause] Trim both leftover rings to the same height... they hold the same volume.
[curious] It's called the napkin-ring theorem. [pause] Punch a cylinder through any sphere — and the leftover band's volume depends only on its height.

[thoughtful] Slice the ring flat. Each slice is an annulus — sphere outer edge, minus cylinder inner edge — and the R-squared cancels. [confident] What's left is pi times h-squared-over-four, minus z-squared. Add the slices... and the ring integrates to pi h cubed over six.
[warm] So a jeweller with a marble... and a giant with a moon — [confident] same-height rings, same amount of stuff.
